qualification.title: T Level Technical Qualification in Digital Software Development (Level 3)
qualification.source_priority_note: Specification and exam papers in docs/source-pdfs are the active source of truth because AGENTS.md and PRODUCT_SPEC.md are empty.

content_areas.title: Problem solving
content_areas.summary: Computational thinking, algorithmic design, and structured approaches to solving programming and process problems.

subtopics.title: Computational thinking
outcomes: Define computational thinking and justify when it should be used.
Apply decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithmic design.
Represent decomposition with flowcharts, code, diagrams, and written descriptions.

subtopics.title: Algorithmic design
outcomes: Interpret, debug, and translate algorithms across flowcharts, written descriptions, and code.
Use sequence, selection, and iteration correctly.
Design algorithms that produce correct outputs for given inputs.

subtopics.title: Problem-solving strategies
outcomes: Compare top-down, bottom-up, and modular approaches.
Apply root-cause analysis techniques such as five whys, FMEA, and ETA.
Use a high-level strategy from problem definition through review.

content_areas.title: Introduction to programming
content_areas.summary: Python 3.10+ programming fundamentals, practical code development, debugging, validation, algorithms, and testing.

subtopics.title: Standard data types
outcomes: Use integers, floats, strings, and Booleans appropriately.
Choose the correct type for a variable or constant in context.

subtopics.title: Variables, constants, and scope
outcomes: Declare variables and constants using standard data types.
Apply local and global scope appropriately.
Use type conversion functions when moving between representations.

subtopics.title: Data structures
outcomes: Interpret and develop code using lists, arrays, and dictionaries.
Debug programs that use structured collections.

subtopics.title: Operators
outcomes: Use arithmetic, relational, and Boolean operators in Python.
Interpret and debug operator-heavy expressions.

subtopics.title: Input and output
outcomes: Handle input via keyboard, screen, and text files.
Open, read, write, and close text files safely.

subtopics.title: Actions: sequence, selection, and iteration
outcomes: Interpret, develop, and debug sequence, selection, and loops.
Use if, else if, else, match/case, for, and while appropriately.

subtopics.title: Functions and procedures
outcomes: Distinguish functions from procedures.
Use user-written, built-in, library, and third-party code.
Interpret, develop, and debug modular code.

subtopics.title: Validation
outcomes: Apply presence, length, range, type, format, and check digit validation.
Interpret, develop, and debug validation logic.

subtopics.title: Programming practices and design decisions
outcomes: Choose data structures and action order for efficiency and maintainability.
Use meaningful names and readable code style conventions.

subtopics.title: Robust code and debugging
outcomes: Handle unexpected input and termination cleanly.
Locate and correct logic and runtime errors.

subtopics.title: Common algorithms
outcomes: Explain linear and binary search.
Explain bubble, insertion, and merge sort.
Judge algorithm suitability using execution time, memory use, and comparisons.

subtopics.title: Testing
outcomes: Select testing methods including unit, system, acceptance, usability, and performance testing.
Create valid, invalid, boundary, and erroneous test data.
Produce structured test plans with expected and actual results.

content_areas.title: Emerging issues and the impact of digital
content_areas.summary: How digital technologies change organisations, society, inclusion, working practices, and the use of AI and emerging platforms.

subtopics.title: Impact of digital technologies
outcomes: Evaluate organisational, societal, and inclusion impacts of digital dependence.
Consider end-user characteristics, accessibility, and digital inclusion.

subtopics.title: Emerging technologies
outcomes: Assess technologies such as IoT, AI, XR, blockchain, quantum computing, and autonomous systems.
Judge organisational, societal, and individual impacts in context.

content_areas.title: Legislation and regulatory requirements
content_areas.summary: Health and safety, data protection, computer misuse, equality, intellectual property, and professional conduct.

subtopics.title: Legislation
outcomes: Explain implications of health and safety, DPA/GDPR, CMA, equality, and intellectual property law.
Make judgements about legal impacts on organisations, society, and individuals.

subtopics.title: Guidelines, standards, and policy
outcomes: Apply codes of conduct, acceptable use policies, whistleblowing, and industry standards.
Link professional behaviour to quality, confidentiality, accessibility, and compliance.

content_areas.title: Business context
content_areas.summary: Organisation types, digital value, business risk, technical change, and project feasibility.

subtopics.title: Business environment
outcomes: Identify organisation types, sectors, business models, and stakeholders.

subtopics.title: Digital value to organisations
outcomes: Explain how digital systems support operations, HR, finance, sales, and management.
Relate system design decisions to user needs and service quality.

subtopics.title: Risk to organisations
outcomes: Explain risks including security, privacy, legal non-compliance, bias, and technical failure.
Assess impact such as fines, reputational harm, and loss of business.

subtopics.title: Technical change management
outcomes: Explain internal and external change triggers.
Use CAB, SMARTER objectives, implementation methods, rollback, and monitoring.

subtopics.title: Digital project feasibility
outcomes: Assess benefits, costs, constraints, and risks when judging feasibility.

content_areas.title: Data
content_areas.summary: Data generation, transformation, quality, storage, models, analysis, and cross-platform access.

subtopics.title: Data, information, and knowledge
outcomes: Distinguish data from information and knowledge.
Explain how humans, sensors, AI, IoT, and transactions generate data.

subtopics.title: Data transformation and taxonomy
outcomes: Explain manipulation, analysis, and processing.
Compare quantitative/qualitative and structured/unstructured data.

subtopics.title: Data types and formats
outcomes: Use data types and formats such as JSON, CSV, XML, UTF-8, and ASCII in context.

subtopics.title: Storage, quality, and maintenance
outcomes: Explain metadata, file and directory structures, Big Data dimensions, and quality assurance methods.

subtopics.title: Data systems and data entry
outcomes: Explain data wrangling, core data system functions, and methods to reduce entry errors.

subtopics.title: Visualisation, models, and access
outcomes: Choose graphs, charts, tables, dashboards, and models appropriately.
Explain hierarchical, network, and relational models plus RBAC, RuBAC, and APIs.

subtopics.title: Data analysis tools
outcomes: Explain data warehouses, lakes, marts, mining, reporting, and business intelligence use.

content_areas.title: Digital environments
content_areas.summary: Hardware, software, networking, virtualisation, cloud, and resilience in technical environments.

subtopics.title: Hardware
outcomes: Explain devices, processors, memory, storage, motherboards, GPUs, NICs, cooling, and sensors.

subtopics.title: Software and development tools
outcomes: Explain OS types, utilities, IDEs, compilers, interpreters, and common application software.

subtopics.title: Networks
outcomes: Explain network types, media, topologies, models, components, packets, protocols, and OSI/TCP-IP.

subtopics.title: Virtual environments
outcomes: Explain virtual machines, hypervisors, benefits, drawbacks, and use cases.

subtopics.title: Cloud environments
outcomes: Compare public and private cloud plus IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.

subtopics.title: Resilient digital environments
outcomes: Explain updates, redundancy, backup strategies, hardening, and hot/cold/warm sites.

content_areas.title: Security
content_areas.summary: Confidentiality, threats, vulnerabilities, mitigation techniques, and security models.

subtopics.title: Confidential information and impact
outcomes: Identify confidential information and explain organisational impact when confidentiality fails.

subtopics.title: Threats and vulnerabilities
outcomes: Explain technical, human, and physical threats and vulnerabilities.

subtopics.title: Threat mitigation
outcomes: Explain anti-malware, encryption, access control, training, backups, VPNs, MFA, and testing.

subtopics.title: CIA and IAAA security models
outcomes: Explain how confidentiality, integrity, and availability interrelate.
Explain identification, authentication, authorisation, and accountability.

tasks.title: Planning a project
tasks.focus: Project planning tools, Gantt chart, resource and cost plan, rationale.
evidence: Decision rationale with risks, benefits, time, and cost impact

tasks.title: Identifying and fixing defects in existing code
tasks.focus: Testing, defect diagnosis, remediation, and evidence capture.

tasks.title: Designing a solution
tasks.focus: Decomposition, algorithms, conventions, and communication of design intent.
evidence: Breakdown of the problem into computational parts
Appropriate notation including flowcharts or code

tasks.title: Developing a solution
tasks.focus: Code organisation, technical skill, user experience, and implementation quality.
evidence: Appropriate handling of data, security, and exceptions
Evidence that the solution meets the brief

tasks.title: Reflective evaluation
tasks.focus: Review how well the product meets requirements and user needs.
evidence: Improvements if the problem were revisited

assessment_objectives.title: English, maths, and digital communication skills

assessment.title: Occupational Specialism: Digital Software Development
performance_outcomes: PO1 Analyse a problem to define requirements and acceptance criteria, aligned to user needs.
PO2 Design, implement and test software.
PO3 Change, maintain and support software.
PO4 Create solutions in a social and collaborative environment.
PO5 Discover, evaluate and apply reliable sources of knowledge.
PO6 Apply ethical principles and manage risks in line with legal and regulatory requirements when developing software.

content_areas.title: Analyse a problem to define requirements and acceptance criteria aligned to user needs
Apply ethical principles and manage risks in line with legal and regulatory requirements
focus: Risk identification, mitigation, contingency, and monitoring

content_areas.title: Discover, evaluate and apply reliable sources of knowledge
focus: Reliability of websites, blogs, papers, forums, and repositories

content_areas.title: Design
focus: Function-oriented, object-oriented, data model, TDD, BDD, and functional design
UX/UI design principles, CMS features, databases, and network integration points

content_areas.title: Create solutions in a social and collaborative environment
focus: Collaborative techniques, code review, paired programming, version control, IDEs, and teamwork

content_areas.title: Implement a solution using at least two appropriate languages
focus: APIs, packages, modules, libraries, and CI/CD
Data sources, responsive UI, deployment methods, and 12-factor principles

content_areas.title: Testing a software solution
focus: Functional, non-functional, front-end, security, manual, and automated testing
Test data, expected results, retests, and regression testing

content_areas.title: Change, maintain and support software
focus: Maintenance drivers, change management, coding principles, and user support
